definition_note: Count the tools/list response of exactly `workspace-mcp --single-user --tools docs drive` (no --tool-tier flag, USER_GOOGLE_EMAIL unset). Tokenize, per tool, the JSON of {name, description, inputSchema}: that is what MCP clients forward to the model; drop title, annotations and outputSchema, which clients keep out of the prompt. Record the per-tool counts as well as the sum. By source count, no tier flag gives 37 tools: 18 in gdocs/docs_tools.py, the 2 document-comment tools, 16 in gdrive/drive_tools.py, and start_google_auth from core/server.py. The user's real configuration runs `--tool-tier complete`, which drops debug_docs_runtime_info (in no tier) and start_google_auth (listed only under gmail), so report the sum both for all tools and without those two. Because USER_GOOGLE_EMAIL is unset, user_google_email stays a required property in every schema, matching the user's setup. The server sends no instructions block in this mode, so there is nothing else to add.

commands.notes: Whole-document plain-text read with default suggestion view; all tabs are concatenated with --- TAB --- separators. Drive files.get + Docs documents.get.
Defaults: include_comments=true, comment_mode=inline, include_resolved=false, so it also pages Drive comments.list. Resolved probe comments from manage_document_comment are excluded from the output.

Graders use this as the index source because inspect_doc_structure fails. It fetches the whole first-tab document but prints only table 0, so output size is constant while latency grows with document size.
Drive-side plain-text export of the native Doc.
Exports the Doc as PDF (default) and, in stdio mode, saves it into the server's local attachment directory; returns the local path. Only local disk is written; nothing is created in Drive.

Lists every comment including resolved ones. Run it before manage_document_comment: each manage_document_comment run leaves one resolved probe comment that this listing then includes, inflating output tokens.
Structured name query, default page_size 10 and detailed output. Matches the five fixture documents; probe files created by this spec use other names so the result set stays stable.
Name-contains search restricted to Google Docs.
Lists the fixture folder. Every create command below adds files to {folder}, so run this before the create commands or record the item count with the result.
Read-only permission listing of the fixture document.
Read-only (2 route uses); returns the existing link and sharing summary without changing permissions.

Typical two-operation batch: insert a 15-character probe at the start of the first tab body and bold it ([1,16) assumes {run} is one digit). The post-write snapshot read fails silently in this build, so the output has no affected-range lines. Undo removes only the exact probe string, so it cannot touch fixture text even if the call failed.

Inserts a probe sentence at body index 1 of the first tab (start of the title paragraph); index 1 is always the first writable body position, so no pre read is needed. modify_doc_text cannot delete without inserting replacement text, so undo deletes the exact probe string with find_and_replace_doc.
Marker phrase 'alpha build' occurs once in the short fixture and 'beta build' does not occur, so the swap is exactly reversible.

Centers the title paragraph (any range inside a paragraph styles the whole paragraph), then sets it back to left. The restore writes an explicit START where the fixture probably inherited START from its named style; the rendered document is identical.

Creates an empty top-level tab after Appendix (index 2 among Tab 1 and Appendix) and deletes it. The tool returns a dict, which arrives as JSON text containing "tab_id": "t.…"; the message field also says 'Tab ID: t.…'. If Google returns no tab ID the capture fails and the probe tab must be removed by hand.

Creates an unanchored document-level comment (this server cannot anchor comments) and resolves it, which posts a visible 'This comment has been resolved.' reply. Comments cannot be deleted with this server, so one resolved probe comment remains per run. The capture is named new_comment to avoid the harness's {comment_id} placeholder, which names the fixture's own thread.
Replaces the existing DEFAULT header text and restores the fixture's exact header text.
Renames the fixture file and restores the name captured from the tool's change report (expected 'Latency fixture short (taylor)'). Only the name changes; no content re-import.

Removing a table needs its end index, which no output reports, so the timed call writes into a scratch doc created by the untimed pre call in {folder} instead of the fixture. The call itself makes 3 API calls (insert table, re-read, populate cells).
